title: Each Domino Is 1.5x Bigger… How Many to Topple a Tower? 🤔
description:
How many dominoes does it take to topple a tower? Lock in a number before the first one lands!

The first domino is 5 cm tall. Every next domino is 1.5 times bigger in every dimension, and each one stands half a domino-height away from the one that will hit it. One flick starts the line: each domino tips over its lower edge, falls under gravity and pushes the next, bigger one. The line ends at a 300 m tower, and the first domino that is taller than the tower knocks it over. The counter shows how many dominoes have toppled so far, the dashed line marks the height of the tower, and a coin, a hand, a person, a house and a tree show the scale as the camera pulls back. Big dominoes fall much more slowly than small ones, so the playback speed changes along the way and is always shown on screen: slow motion at the start, fast forward for the giants.
This is a simplified rigid-block model: every domino is a solid block that pivots on its edge, contact is frictionless and does not bounce, and the tower is treated as a lighter block. Physics, picture and sound are generated by code (seed 39), with no footage, samples or stock media.
What number did you guess?
#simulation #satisfying #dominoes
